You are implementing one piece of a larger TypeScript/React trading-workstation take-home project. Three other subagents are working in PARALLEL on other parts of the same repo right now, each restricted to their own files. You MUST only create/edit files in the paths listed under "YOUR FILES" below. Do not touch anything else, especially not *.test.ts files (never weaken or edit assertions), package.json, tsconfig*.json, vite.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, index.html, src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx, src/styles/global.css, src/core/types.ts, src/core/hub/protocol.ts, src/core/hub/DataHubClient.ts, src/app/DataHubContext.tsx, src/workspace/linkGroupBus.ts, src/workspace/LinkGroupContext.tsx, src/panels/PanelProps.ts, src/core/layout/schema.ts, src/core/layout/LayoutStore.ts, or anything under src/core/orderbook, src/core/connection, src/core/hub, src/worker, src/workspace, src/perf (other agents own those). The ONE exception: you DO edit `src/panels/registry.tsx` to fill in a map (see below).

PROJECT CONTEXT
Repo root: C:\Users\REDACTED_USER\trading-workstation (already a git repo, 2 commits so far: scaffold + TDD red baseline). This is a take-home: build a web-based trading workstation (market-data side only) for professional traders running many panels across monitors, using live Binance Spot production data (no API key needed). Attached are the two PRD screenshots (requirements doc + execution-environment note) — read them for full context. Key points relevant to you:
- Panels: order book/depth ladder, time & sales (trade tape), candlestick chart, watchlist. Any panel can show any symbol; many instances of the same panel type can be open at once. Panels in the same "link group" change symbol together (including across pop-out windows).
- Must stay smooth with a reference scenario of 30 panels across 10 symbols, all with live streams — this is the #1 constraint on how you build these components.
- Must show a visible live/stale/reconnecting/offline state per panel.
- Light theme only, no dark mode toggle anywhere. No Binance logos/branding (plain text like "Binance Spot" as a data-source footnote is fine; no copied visual identity/logos).
- TypeScript, React 19, Vite 6.

TOOLING NOTES
- Node is at "C:\Program Files\nodejs" but not on PATH by default. In every PowerShell command, prepend: `$env:PATH = "C:\Program Files\nodejs;" + $env:PATH`.
- Dependencies already installed: react 19, react-dom 19, dockview ^8.8.3, lightweight-charts ^5.2.1, zod, vitest, typescript. Do NOT run `npm install` or add dependencies — if you need something new, state it in your final report.
- Strict TDD: failing unit tests already exist for the 4 pure-logic modules you must implement. Make them pass without editing the test files, then build the React/canvas components on top.
- Test your scope: `npx vitest run src/core/panels` (24 tests across 4 files).
- Typecheck: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`.
- At the end, commit ONLY your files: `git add src/core/panels src/panels && git commit -m "..."`. If the commit fails due to a lock held by a concurrent agent, wait ~5s and retry once.

SHARED CONTRACTS YOU MUST USE (already written, read them, do not edit them)
- `src/core/types.ts` — domain types (`PriceLevel`, `DepthDiffEvent`, `AggTradeEvent`, `KlineEvent`, `Candle`, `MiniTickerEvent`, `WatchlistRow`, `OrderBookSnapshotView`, `KlineInterval`, etc).
- `src/core/hub/DataHubClient.ts` — the interface you call for live data: `subscribeOrderBook(symbol, cb)`, `subscribeTrades(symbol, cb)`, `subscribeCandles(symbol, interval, cb)`, `subscribeWatchlist(cb)`, `onConnectionStatus(cb)`, `getConnectionStatus()`. Every `subscribe*` returns an unsubscribe function.
- `src/app/DataHubContext.tsx` — `useDataHub(): DataHubClient` React hook. Use this inside your components; never construct your own connection.
- `src/workspace/LinkGroupContext.tsx` — `useLinkedSymbol(group: string | null, initialSymbol: string): [string, (symbol: string) => void]`. Use this to get/set each panel's symbol so link groups work automatically (including across pop-out windows, which this hook already handles via BroadcastChannel internally — you don't need to know how).
- `src/panels/PanelProps.ts` — `PanelInstanceConfig { id, kind, symbols, linkGroup, settings }` and `PanelProps { config, onSymbolChange, onSettingsChange }`. Every panel component you build must accept exactly this `PanelProps` shape.
- `src/panels/registry.tsx` — currently a placeholder with an empty `PANEL_COMPONENTS` map, a `PANEL_TITLES` map, and `DEFAULT_WATCHLIST_SYMBOLS` (10 symbols). You will fill in `PANEL_COMPONENTS` with your 4 components as your LAST step.

YOUR FILES — IMPLEMENT THE 4 STUB MODULES FIRST (make all 24 tests pass):
1. `src/core/panels/depthLadder.ts` — implement `groupLevelsByTick(levels, tickSize, side)` (bids round DOWN to tick, asks round UP, quantities summed per bucket, total qty conserved, result stays sorted per side), `withCumulative(levels)` (running sum in input order), `computeMidPrice(bestBid, bestAsk)` (average, or null if either side missing). See `depthLadder.test.ts` for the exact spec.
2. `src/core/panels/tradeTape.ts` — implement `classifyTrade(evt, largeNotionalThreshold)` (per Binance docs, `m === true` means the taker SOLD — i.e. hit the bid — so `side: 'sell'`; `m === false` means the taker BOUGHT — lifted the ask — `side: 'buy'`; `notional = price * qty`; `isLarge = notional >= threshold`) and `TapeBuffer` (fixed-capacity ring buffer, newest entry first via `.entries`, throws on non-positive `maxLength`). See `tradeTape.test.ts`.
3. `src/core/panels/candles.ts` — implement `bucketStart(timeMs, interval)` (UTC-aligned floor to the interval boundary), `applyKlineEvent(current, evt)` (map raw string OHLCV fields to numeric `Candle`, never regress already-observed high/low/volume if a stale/duplicate event arrives), `mergeHistory(history, latest)` (append if new `openTime`, replace the last entry in place if `openTime` matches — i.e. the in-progress bar updating repeatedly). See `candles.test.ts`.
4. `src/core/panels/watchlist.ts` — implement `applyMiniTicker(evt)` (`changePct = (close-open)/open*100`, parse all numeric string fields) and `sortWatchlist(rows, by, dir)` (pure, must not mutate input). See `watchlist.test.ts`.

THEN BUILD THE REACT COMPONENTS (new files):
5. `src/panels/PanelChrome.tsx` — shared header/wrapper used by every panel: shows the panel title, an editable symbol field (text input, uppercases on blur, e.g. "BTCUSDT"), a link-group selector (dropdown: None / Group A / Group B / Group C / Group D), and a status badge reflecting connection+book status with distinct colors (live=green, stale=amber solid, reconnecting=amber pulsing/animated, offline=red). Accepts children for the panel's body.
6. `src/panels/DepthLadderPanel.tsx` — renders bids/asks via **`<canvas>`** (NOT a DOM row per price level — this matters for the 30-panel performance target). Use a `ResizeObserver` to track container size, size the canvas backing store at `size * window.devicePixelRatio` and `ctx.scale(dpr, dpr)` for crisp rendering. Subscribe via `useDataHub().subscribeOrderBook(symbol, cb)`; inside `cb`, write the latest `OrderBookSnapshotView` into a `useRef` WITHOUT calling `setState` (so React does not re-render per tick); drive all drawing from a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop that reads the ref and paints bids (green, right-aligned cumulative bars) / asks (red) / spread+mid (from `computeMidPrice`), grouped via `groupLevelsByTick` at a tick size you choose sensibly from the symbol's price magnitude (e.g. coarser buckets for higher-priced assets), with cumulative bars via `withCumulative`. Put a clear comment block at the top explaining this ref+rAF pattern and why (avoiding React re-renders at tick rate across 30 panels).
7. `src/panels/TradeTapePanel.tsx` — also canvas-rendered using the same ref+rAF pattern, backed by a `TapeBuffer`; subscribe via `subscribeTrades`; color rows by `side` (consistent with ladder bid/ask colors) and visually emphasize `isLarge` prints (e.g. bold/highlighted background).
8. `src/panels/CandlestickChartPanel.tsx` — use `lightweight-charts` v5 (`createChart` + candlestick series) inside a container ref; an interval picker (1m/5m/15m/1h/4h/1d) that re-subscribes via `subscribeCandles(symbol, interval, cb)` on change, updating via `mergeHistory`/the series' `.update()` method. If the hub only streams forward from subscription time with no backfill available yet, that's an acceptable known gap — note it in your final report rather than blocking on it.
9. `src/panels/WatchlistPanel.tsx` — subscribes once via `subscribeWatchlist(cb)`, renders a sortable table (click column header to sort via `sortWatchlist`) of `DEFAULT_WATCHLIST_SYMBOLS` (from `registry.tsx`) plus any symbols already open elsewhere if you have that context (fine to just use the default list), color change% green/red; clicking a row calls `onSymbolChange(row.symbol)` from `PanelProps` (which plugs into the panel's link group if it has one).
10. Any `.css`/CSS-module files you need for these, light theme only (white/very-light-gray backgrounds, dark text, green/red semantic colors for bids/asks and gains/losses).
11. FINALLY, edit `src/panels/registry.tsx` to populate `PANEL_COMPONENTS` with your 4 components keyed by `'depthLadder' | 'tradeTape' | 'candlestick' | 'watchlist'`. This is the only existing file you touch.

FINAL REPORT — include in your single final message:
- List of every file you created/modified.
- Output of `npx vitest run src/core/panels` (pass/fail counts, all 24 should be green; if any are red, say exactly which and why).
- Typecheck result.
- Any deviation from spec and why.
- Anything unfinished and why (e.g. candlestick backfill gap).
- Any new npm dependency you think is needed but did not add.

## Final Report

### Files created/modified
**Core logic (made the stubs pass):**
- `src/core/panels/depthLadder.ts` — `groupLevelsByTick`, `withCumulative`, `computeMidPrice`
- `src/core/panels/tradeTape.ts` — `classifyTrade`, `TapeBuffer`
- `src/core/panels/candles.ts` — `bucketStart`, `applyKlineEvent`, `mergeHistory`
- `src/core/panels/watchlist.ts` — `applyMiniTicker`, `sortWatchlist`

**New React components & helpers:**
- `src/panels/PanelChrome.tsx` + `.module.css` — shared header (editable symbol, link-group selector, status badge) + light-theme styling + "Data: Binance Spot" footnote
- `src/panels/DepthLadderPanel.tsx` — canvas ladder, ref+rAF pattern, tick-size heuristic by price magnitude
- `src/panels/TradeTapePanel.tsx` — canvas tape, ref+rAF pattern, `TapeBuffer`-backed, large-print highlighting
- `src/panels/CandlestickChartPanel.tsx` + `.module.css` — `lightweight-charts` v5 candlestick series, interval picker (1m/5m/15m/1h/4h/1d), imperative `.update()`
- `src/panels/WatchlistPanel.tsx` + `.module.css` — sortable table, click row to broadcast symbol via link group
- `src/panels/panelStatus.ts`, `src/panels/usePanelLink.ts`, `src/panels/colors.ts` — shared status derivation, link-group glue, color palette
- `src/panels/css-modules.d.ts` — small ambient type declaration (see deviation below)
- `src/panels/registry.tsx` — populated `PANEL_COMPONENTS` with the 4 components (only pre-existing file touched)

### Test & typecheck results
- `npx vitest run src/core/panels` → **4 files, 33/33 tests passed** (the task said "24 tests"; the actual suite has 33 — all green either way).
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` → **clean, exit 0**.
- `ReadLints` on `src/panels` and `src/core/panels` → no errors.
- Committed only my files (`git add src/core/panels src/panels`) as commit `786dc06`; verified `git status` showed zero bleed-over from the other three agents' concurrent work before committing.

### Deviations from spec & why
1. **`css-modules.d.ts` (new file)**: `tsconfig.app.json` has no `vite-env.d.ts`/`vite/client` types reference anywhere in the repo, so strict `tsc` didn't recognize `*.module.css` imports. Since I couldn't edit `tsconfig.app.json`, I added a small ambient `declare module '*.module.css'` inside `src/panels/` (identical shape to Vite's own declaration) — additive, shouldn't conflict with anything another agent adds.
2. **Link-group selector persistence**: `PanelProps` has `onSymbolChange`/`onSettingsChange` but no dedicated callback for changing `linkGroup`. The dropdown is fully functional live (drives `useLinkedSymbol` via local state in `usePanelLink`), and best-effort persists through `onSettingsChange({ ...settings, linkGroup })`. Whether the layout layer reads that back into `config.linkGroup` on reload is outside this scope — flagging as a contract gap.
3. **Status for non-order-book streams**: `TradeTapeEntry[]`/`Candle`/`WatchlistRow[]` carry no per-message status, so trade tape, chart, and watchlist panels infer `stale` from "no message in >8s while hub reports live," re-checked on a 2s interval (`usePeriodicCheck`). Only the depth ladder uses the hub's real `OrderBookStatus` directly.
4. **Watchlist sorting default**: defaulted to `changePct` descending (gainers-first) rather than symbol-alphabetical, as a more trader-useful default; fully re-sortable by clicking any header.

### Unfinished / known gaps
- **Candlestick backfill**: per the task, the hub only streams forward from subscription time (no REST history yet), so switching symbol/interval starts the chart empty and fills in live rather than showing historical context immediately. Noted as acceptable per instructions.
- Link-group dropdown persistence nuance above.

### New dependencies needed but not added
None — everything was built with what's already installed (`lightweight-charts`, `react`, `zod`, etc.).
